references.label: Hamming observed production median
references.boundary: Median latency observed across more than 10 million minutes of production calls. The start and end instants are not restated beside the figure.
references.placement: No boundary is stated with it, so it is read on the widest Callstorm clock: an agent under this range from true end of speech is under it on any narrower clock too.

references.label: Coval p95 target under load
references.boundary: Response latency under load, p95 under 2s. The start and end instants are not defined beside the threshold.
references.placement: No boundary is stated with it, so it is read on the widest Callstorm clock, where holding it means holding it on any narrower one.

references.label: Hamming TTFW breakdown line
references.boundary: TTFW, from VAD silence detection to the first agent audio byte. Past 800ms is conversation breakdown. No percentile is stated.
references.placement: Its clock starts at detection, so it is read on think/speak. Callstorm's detection instant is the agent's transcript arriving, later than VAD detection by transcript finalization, so this reading leans in the agent's favour.

references.label: Human turn-taking marker
references.boundary: People answer about 208ms after the other speaker stops, across languages. 300ms is the edge Hamming labels natural.
references.placement: A human gap runs from the moment the other speaker actually stops, so it is read on the end-of-speech clock at the median. It marks what a person does; it is not a pass line.
